name: Suvorexant
route_note: Oral tablet within 30 minutes of bedtime, with at least 7 hours remaining before waking.

discovery.by: Merck Research Laboratories (Cox, Coleman and colleagues)
discovery.note: Developed after the 1998 discovery of the orexin (hypocretin) neuropeptides and their role in wakefulness, via high-throughput screening and optimisation of a diazepane series.

tagline: First orexin receptor antagonist for insomnia, switching off a wake-promoting signal
summary: Suvorexant is the first approved dual orexin receptor antagonist, used for insomnia characterised by difficulty falling or staying asleep. Rather than enhancing GABA-mediated sedation, it blocks the wake-promoting orexin system.
mechanism: Orexin A and B, made by neurons in the lateral hypothalamus, stabilise wakefulness by activating OX1 and OX2 receptors on monoaminergic and cholinergic arousal centres. Loss of orexin neurons causes narcolepsy.
Suvorexant reversibly blocks both orexin receptors, reducing the drive for wakefulness and allowing sleep to occur, with less disruption of sleep architecture than GABA-A modulators.
uses: Insomnia with difficulty in sleep onset and/or sleep maintenance in adults

history.title: Orexins discovered
history.detail: Two groups (de Lecea/Sutcliffe and Sakurai/Yanagisawa) independently identify the hypocretin/orexin neuropeptides.

history.title: Link to narcolepsy
history.detail: Orexin receptor mutations cause canine narcolepsy and knockout mice show narcolepsy.

history.title: Compound reported
history.detail: Merck publishes the discovery of MK-4305 (suvorexant).

history.title: FDA review
history.detail: An advisory committee and FDA request lower starting doses than Merck proposed.

history.title: Approvals
history.detail: Suvorexant is approved in Japan and, in August 2014, by the FDA as Belsomra.

history.title: Alzheimer's insomnia
history.detail: Labelling is updated to include efficacy in insomnia in people with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.

facts: Lemborexant and daridorexant are later dual orexin receptor antagonists.
